collection.description: A villager tied half the nets on this island.

ask.text:
(subject) tied half the nets on this island. (subject.His/Her) knots are famous. Young fishers used to watch (subject.his/her) fingers fly and try to copy them, and fail.
Lately, those fingers fumble. Knots that used to take a blink now take a long, painful minute. (subject.His/Her) knuckles ache in the mornings and swell in the damp. And (subject) has started hiding the knotting work under a mat whenever anyone walks past, pretending to be doing something else.
(young) noticed today. (subject.He/She) saw the half-finished net, and the mat, and (subject)'s face when (subject.he/she) realized (subject.he/she) had been seen. (young) doesn't want to embarrass (subject.him/her), but (subject.he/she) can't pretend (subject.he/she) didn't see it either. What should (young) do?

choices.label: Ask How They Want to Fish

c1o1.text: (subject) thinks about it for a long time. Then (subject.he/she) decides (subject.he/she) will keep fishing by hand line from the rocks, which is gentle on the fingers and always has been (subject.his/her) favourite anyway. It's a choice that is (subject.his/hers) alone. The next morning, (subject.he/she) is out on the rocks at dawn, and comes back with three fish and a smug expression.

c1o2.text: (subject) is quiet for a while. Then, without looking at anyone, (subject.he/she) slides the mat off the half-finished net and asks for help with the knotting. (subject.His/Her) family, who thought pride would never allow it, are so surprised that no one says anything at all for a moment. Then everyone sits down at once, and the net is finished by evening.

c1.text: (young) sits down beside (subject) and asks, very simply, "What would you like to keep doing?"...

c2o1.text: (subject) teaches (young) seven net knots, slowly, and the reason behind each one: this one for deep water, this one so a torn net doesn't unravel, this one to hold a weight. (young)'s head is spinning by sunset, but (subject.he/she) can tie all seven. (subject) watches (subject.him/her) do it, nods once, and says nothing, which from (subject) is the highest praise.

c2o2.text: Halfway through, (subject) stops. There's one old knot, the "crab claw", that (subject.he/she) can't quite remember any more. (subject.He/She) tries three times, gets it wrong three times, and finally asks the other old fishers to help puzzle it out. It takes them the whole evening, a great deal of arguing, and a lot of string.

c2.text: (young) asks if (subject) would teach (subject.him/her) the knots, all of them, before they're forgotten. (subject) frowns, then cracks (subject.his/her) aching knuckles. "Sit down. Watch my hands. Not my face, my HANDS."...

c3o1.text: The frame holds the net steady, and (subject)'s fingers only have to do the knotting, not the holding. (subject.He/She) ties knots in comfort again, slowly but surely, and seems genuinely moved. "Huh," (subject.he/she) says gruffly. "Not bad." The frame stays by (subject.his/her) hut for the rest of (subject.his/her) life.

c3o2.text: (subject) tries the frame, but (subject.his/her) hands are hurting too much today. So (subject.he/she) soaks them in a bowl of warm water instead, and leaves the nets for tomorrow. (young) sits with (subject.him/her) while (subject.he/she) does, and they talk about the sea.

c3.text: (young) has an idea, and spends the afternoon building a wooden frame that can hold a net steady at just the right height, so (subject) doesn't have to grip it...
